exposure: neonatal characteristics (e.g., low birth weight, prematurity, cesarean section, mechanical ventilation, tachycardia, hemoglobin, platelets, stroke, unexpected delivery, respiratory distress, convulsive crisis, procalcitonin, urea, AST/TGO levels)
cohort: The study participants were 314 neonates diagnosed with sepsis identified from 8382 neonatal clinical records at a tertiary hospital in northwestern Mexico.
finding: The study found that various neonatal characteristics, including low birth weight, prematurity, and cesarean section, were associated with multidrug-resistant microorganisms, while others like low birth weight and mechanical ventilation were associated with mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with extensively drug-resistant (XDR) or multidrug-resistant (MDR) microorganisms.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was a characteristic analyzed.
